CausalChain: Green tea catechins (EGCG) -> Modulation of IL-8 and related signaling pathways -> Disruption of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in cancer stem cells -> Energy depletion and metabolic stress -> Induction of apoptosis and impaired self-renewal -> Selective elimination of cancer stem cells
Hypothesis: EGCG-rich green tea catechins selectively compromise the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in cancer stem cells, inducing metabolic stress that triggers apoptosis and reduces self-renewal, thereby potentially preventing cancer metastasis and recurrence.
Abstract: We propose that green tea catechins, particularly EGCG, not only exert broad anticancer effects but also selectively target cancer stem cells by disrupting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. In our hypothesis, EGCG modulates signaling pathways such as IL-8 that control metabolic flux and mitochondrial efficiency in cancer stem cells. This disruption creates a metabolic vulnerability that leads to energy depletion, induction of cell cycle arrest, and subsequent apoptosis of these resilient cells. The proposed mechanism could offer a novel therapeutic target to prevent metastasis and tumor recurrence when used as an adjunct to conventional treatments.
